recommendation_summary: The reply recommends replacing the in-memory row and object counting with a filtered COUNT(*) in the existing Postgres database, backed by an index on the unpaid predicate. It adds no new infrastructure and keeps request-time committed-data freshness. Kafka, CQRS and Redis are rejected outright, not offered as options. It ends by asking the user to confirm. The one-second target is reasoned about but not verified.

labels.Requirements and who asked: Fast unpaid count reflecting committed invoices from portal need; Kafka/CQRS/Redis from you citing approved budget and peer practice
labels.Deleted: Kafka cluster, topics and services, CQRS projection, Redis for this count
labels.Bottleneck: Loading invoice rows and building objects in app memory to count
labels.Checked myself: Single app and Postgres and count-only endpoint with no other reader, as you told me

note: All four record lines come before the recommendation and are specific to this decision. The Kafka/CQRS/Redis stack is named and removed, and Checked myself says its facts came from the user rather than from any test or inspection.
